f606W.note: 2026-09-15: two real features near the quad are deliberately LEFT UNMASKED. (1) col 185, row 106 (r=2.25", 1.4 theta_E) is the FOURTH IMAGE of this cusp quad, not a cosmic ray: detected in F606W/F814W/F438W at the same sky position to 0.4 px (peak per-pixel S/N 26.0/9.4/8.2), broader than the PSF (sigma 0.076" vs 0.055"; CRs are sharper), tangentially elongated (b/a 0.41, 89 deg from radial), and at the radius the Shu+2016 model predicts for image 4 (2.16"). (2) The diffuse patch ~0.9" from it (col 163-170, row 92-100, r~2.3") is REAL but its nature is OPEN: positive in all four input flc frames (145/111/236/182 e, 2.3-5.0 sigma each, no CR flags) where a blank-sky control scatters about zero, +7.9 sigma over the local floor in F606W, colour like the arc (F606W/F814W ~2.2 vs 2.9 for image 4) -- but elongated only 33 deg from radial, and de-lensing it puts its source 0.4" from the real source. Its required counter-image (col 163, row 173, mu=0.9) is 3x fainter than the patch, so its absence proves nothing. Fit with it in, inspect the residual, mask only if the reconstruction cannot produce it.

f160W.note: 2026-09-13: UNCERTAIN -- the user flags J1020+1122's masks as uncertain in general and f160W MOST of all; treat this band's boundary as provisional and refit with it varied before quoting anything sensitive to it. The mask SIZE is not the doubt (two large nearby galaxies really do contaminate the right of the frame) -- where the edge falls is. All three bands were drawn fresh, each rejecting the f814W proposal outright (n_erased_px 0), and they disagree: 67.93 arcsec2 excluded in f814W, 53.39 in f606W, 66.10 here, i.e. f606W excludes ~21% less sky than f814W for the same contaminants.

f606W.note: 2026-09-13: masks a SECOND weakly-sheared background galaxy, object B, at dRA -3.67 dDec +1.43 (sky NW), r=3.94" -- distinct from the red object A at r=3.68" that the f814W note covers. Not an arc and not part of A. A and B have OPPOSITE colours (A redder than the deflector, B bluer: f606W/f814W relative to the lens 0.30 vs 1.42), which rules out the fold-pair reading two objects at the same radius would otherwise invite -- two images of one source must share a colour. No counter-image (f606W S/N -0.2 at B's mirror position vs 3.7 at B). Its tangential elongation (b/a 0.75 at 82 deg from radial in f814W, 0.56 at 70 deg in f606W) matches the 0.71 weak shear predicts at that radius for theta_E 1.35". B is faint (S/N 5-6) so the shape is noisy; the counter-image null and the radius carry the argument. B is detected in all three bands but is masked ONLY here -- add it to f814W when that mask is next touched.

f814W.note: 2026-09-13: the compact red object 3.68" from the deflector is NOT an arc and is masked. It is tangentially elongated (b/a 0.70, major axis 89 deg from radial), which is why it reads as one, but that is weak shear, not strong lensing: no counter-image anywhere at 2.5-5.5", and it is ~3x REDDER than the deflector (f160W/f814W) where a lensed SLACS source would be bluer. The implied shear gives theta_E ~1.3-1.4", matching the faint f606W knots at r=1.4-1.8" that are the real lensed features. See diagnostics/J1016+3859_f814W_arc_test.png. A second sheared galaxy, object B, sits at r=3.94" (sky NW) and is masked in f606W but NOT here, though it is detected in f814W at S/N ~5; see the f606W note.

2026-09-14: pulled back off the expected arc radius -- cleared masked pixels within 1.2" of the deflector (3147 -> 3123 px). Bolton 2008 gives sigma=213+/-17 km/s, z_l=0.1888, z_s=0.4730 -> SIS theta_E=0.75", and that estimator runs ~30-40% low against rings measured in this repo, so the arc is expected near ~1.0". The mask previously reached 1.06", i.e. onto that radius. No arc is actually detected here (no blue excess anywhere in f606W/f814W) and the masked companion at r=1.77" is ~1.8x theta_E, so it is very unlikely to be the lensed source -- this is precautionary clearance, not a correction.
